notes: Expanded sensor array with sixth sensor at center front and wider lateral spacing to improve sharp turn coverage and line detection. Reduced kp to 6 to smooth steering and reduce oscillation, maintaining other PID gains. Observation requests cover key performance and control metrics.
rationale: The previous iteration's evidence shows that increasing sensor size to 0.016 m and shifting sensors forward improved line coverage and early detection, reducing line loss events on oval and s-bend tracks. However, the slalom track still has very low finish rates and relatively high steering oscillation, indicating challenges with sharp turns and control stability. To address this, I adjusted sensor x-positions outward by ±0.01 m to better cover sharp turns on the slalom track and added a sixth sensor at the center front (x=0, y=0.07) to improve line detection in challenging sections. I reduced the proportional gain kp from 8 to 6 to smooth steering control and reduce oscillation, as prior evidence shows lower kp can help with control stability. Sensor size, wheel radius, wheel track, body dimensions, and mass remain unchanged to maintain stability and handling. The controller uses PID gains tuned for smoother control, with sensor weights emphasizing outer sensors and the new center front sensor for improved edge detection and early line detection. The line loss recovery strategy remains 'search_left' to steer right when the line is lost. Observation requests include completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, steering_oscillation, and control_effort to monitor performance and control smoothness comprehensively.
